metaTitle: Free Trucking Invoice Template — No Signup, No Watermark
metaDescription: Free trucking invoice template for owner-operators and carriers — no signup, no watermark. Download an editable Word and PDF invoice or build one online.
intro: This is a free trucking invoice template made for owner-operators, carriers, and freight haulers who bill brokers and shippers per load or per mile. It has room for the trip and BOL numbers, the pickup and delivery points, and the rate, so a broker can match your invoice to the load and pay it fast.

It is completely free, with no signup and no watermark. Download the editable Word and PDF files and fill them in on your own computer, or use the generator below to build a freight invoice in the browser and download a print-ready PDF in minutes.
included: A load or trip reference, BOL (bill of lading) number, and pickup and delivery locations, so a broker can tie the invoice to the exact shipment
Line items for the freight charge (flat rate or per-mile), fuel surcharge, and accessorials like detention, layover, or lumper fees
A header for your business name, logo, MC/DOT number, and contact details, plus a bill-to section for the broker or shipper
A unique invoice number with issue and due dates so every load is easy to track and follow up on
Automatic subtotal, tax, and grand total, plus a notes and payment-terms area for quick-pay, factoring, or Net 30 terms
Free editable Word and PDF files, print-ready on one page, with no watermark and no signup

steps.title: Add your carrier, broker, and load details
steps.body: Enter your company name, logo, MC/DOT number, and contact info at the top, then add the broker or shipper you are billing. Fill in the load or trip number, the BOL, and the pickup and delivery points, and give the invoice a unique number with issue and due dates.

steps.title: Enter the freight charge and any extras
steps.body: Add the line haul as a flat rate or miles times your rate per mile, then list a fuel surcharge and any accessorials — detention, layover, or a lumper fee. The template adds up line totals, subtotal, tax, and the grand total for you.

steps.title: Download and send
steps.body: Download a print-ready PDF (or the editable Word file) and email it to the broker or shipper with the signed BOL and rate confirmation attached. Note your payment terms — quick-pay, factoring, or Net 30 — and how you want to be paid.

faqs.q: What should I attach to a freight invoice so the broker pays it?
faqs.a: Most brokers want the invoice sent with the signed bill of lading (proof of delivery) and the rate confirmation for that load. Put the load or trip number and BOL number on the invoice so they line up with the paperwork, and email everything together. Missing or mismatched documents are the most common reason a trucking invoice gets held up.

faqs.q: How do I invoice per mile versus a flat rate?
faqs.a: Both work on the same template. For a flat rate, add one line for the line haul with the agreed amount. For per-mile pay, put the miles as the quantity and your rate per mile as the unit price, and the template calculates the line total. Add the fuel surcharge and any accessorials as separate lines so the broker sees the full breakdown.

faqs.q: How does this work with a factoring company?
faqs.a: If you factor your invoices, you still create the invoice the same way, but you send it to the factoring company instead of collecting from the broker yourself. Add the factor's notice-of-assignment or remit-to details in the notes and payment-terms area so the broker knows to pay the factor. The template stays free to use whether you factor or bill direct.

faqs.q: Is the template really free with no watermark?
faqs.a: Yes. The Word and PDF files are free to download and use, with no signup and no watermark. You can reuse them for every load and broker and edit them however you like.
